title: Mercor's Indian-Origin Founders Double Wealth to $4.2 Billion Each at 23
excerpt: A $750 million funding round valuing AI hiring startup Mercor at $20 billion has lifted Forbes' estimates for co-founders Adarsh Hiremath and Surya Midha, and CEO Brendan Foody, to about $4.2 billion each.
body:
• AI startup Mercor has raised $750 million in a fresh funding round that values the company at $20 billion, with Benchmark, General Catalyst, Nvidia and Salesforce among the investors, NDTV reported.
  • Forbes estimates each of the three 23-year-old co-founders — CEO Brendan Foody, CTO Adarsh Hiremath and chairman Surya Midha — is now worth about $4.2 billion, based on stakes of about 21% each.
  • That is roughly double their estimated $2.2 billion each in October 2025, when Mercor was valued at $10 billion after a $350 million round.
  • The figures are Forbes estimates of paper wealth in a private company, not realised cash; the founders' fortunes move with Mercor's valuation.

The three co-founders of Mercor have doubled their estimated fortunes in about a year. The AI hiring startup raised $750 million in a funding round announced on Tuesday that values the company at $20 billion, and Forbes now estimates CEO Brendan Foody, chief technology officer Adarsh Hiremath and board chairman Surya Midha at about $4.2 billion each, based on stakes of roughly 21% apiece, according to NDTV's report of the Forbes estimates. Investors in the round included Benchmark, General Catalyst, Nvidia and Salesforce.

Reported versus estimated

The reported facts are the raise and the $20 billion valuation. The $4.2 billion fortunes are Forbes estimates derived from those stakes — the standard way private-company founder wealth is calculated, and a number that exists on paper until shares can be sold. The same method put the three at about $2.2 billion each in October 2025, when a $350 million round valued Mercor at $10 billion.

"Reported versus estimated The reported facts are the raise and the $20 billion valuation."

From a San Jose debate team to the youngest self-made billionaires

Hiremath and Midha are Indian-Americans who attended Bellarmine College Preparatory, an all-boys school in San Jose, California, where they were on the debate team together. Midha, a second-generation immigrant whose parents moved to the US from New Delhi, was born in Mountain View and raised in San Jose, and dropped out of Georgetown University; Hiremath studied computer science at Harvard for two years before leaving, according to earlier Forbes reporting summarised by Inshorts. The three founded Mercor in 2023 and became the world's youngest self-made billionaires at 22, passing Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan, who was 27, and Mark Zuckerberg, who became a billionaire at 23.

The speed of the repricing is the story in the numbers: $10 billion in October 2025, $20 billion now, with two funding rounds — $350 million, then $750 million — in between. Each round has been led or joined by established venture firms, and the presence of Nvidia and Salesforce in the latest round puts two large technology companies on the investor list alongside Benchmark and General Catalyst.

What Mercor does

Mercor, founded as a platform connecting software engineers from India and other emerging markets with US tech companies, now works in AI talent and data work for major AI labs, according to Forbes' earlier reporting. What to watch next is the usual test for a private valuation of this size: whether revenue and hiring demand keep pace with a price that has doubled in roughly a year, and what any future round or public listing does to the paper fortunes it has created.
